findings.summary: The new rule that the inviter stays anonymous until acceptance contradicts InvitePreview, which shows the recipient who is inviting them before they Accept or Decline.
findings.evidence: Diff: "Opening the invitation does not reveal who sent it until it has been accepted" vs component.InvitePreview: "The recipient sees who is inviting them" (cardinality: exactly one after validation, i.e. before acceptance)

findings.summary: Journey step s7 has the invitee see the inviter before choosing Accept or Decline, which conflicts with the new anonymity claim the consent criterion and fixture now test.
findings.evidence: J.connect s7: "See who is inviting; Accept or Decline" vs C.webapp.connection.consent claim: "an unaccepted invitation never reveals the inviter"

findings.summary: Hiding the inviter's identity until after acceptance means the invitee consents to a pair without knowing who the other party is, which undermines the explicit two-party consent the feature and policy require.
findings.evidence: GD.connect: "Invitation-based pairs formed by two explicit consents; the inviter stays anonymous until acceptance"; policy.pairConsent: "creating the invitation and accepting it provide the two consents"
